messages.subject: A newbie's question
parts:
Hi,
Shiny is a real wonder and I love working in it.Being a newbie to Shiny, I have some questions to be quenched. Is it possible to build a website in shiny?? All examples that I have come across has just a single page. My application requires authentication of users and navigate to a page respective to the type of user. Is there a way to do all of this in a single Rscript in Shiny or at least link different a Rscripts??

messages.author: 3a4c7d2513de18a2
messages.subject: Re: A newbie's question
parts:
On Thursday, April 11, 2013 4:09:48 AM UTC+2, Leela Manju wrote:
Shiny is a real wonder and I love working in it.Being a newbie to Shiny, I have some questions to be quenched. Is it possible to build a website in shiny?? All examples that I have come across has just a single page. My application requires authentication of users and navigate to a page

You can build a website using html-ui approach:
http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#html-ui

The frontend contains the usual components you use for your frontend stack.
The backend contains server.R and the other components for controllers / routes.

The link between the frontend and server.R are the name attribute for the inputs and shiny-html-output, shiny-text-output and shiny-plot-output classes for the outputs.

Hope that helps,
Alberto

You should build your site as usual, using the stack you prefer.

For instance, if you use a MV* approach, you need to define the controllers and routes to navigate in the app.
See, for instance, opinionated frameworks as Backbone.js or Angular.js.

Then, when a page needs to communicate with R backend, you add Shiny "components": the script (shiny.js), the names and classes for ins and outs.

Are you be able to navigate between the pages without Shiny? Use the same approach after you "shined" the pages. :)

Regards,
Alberto

As Alberto mentioned, the tutorial shows how to make a page that has the user interface side written completely in HTML, instead of ui.r.

If you still want to use ui.r, you could use the htmlOutput() function if you want to just send pieces of HTML to the client.

In server.r, you'd do something like:
  output$something <- renderText({
     "<p>text here</p>"
  })


And in ui.r:
  htmlOutput("something")

-Winston
